title: Why a click can feel slow
purpose: See how a busy main thread delays the next paint after a click, and how the Performance panel records it.
sequence_reason: A click, the work it starts and the next paint happen in a fixed order, so motion shows the delay better than one picture.
summary: An intro to the Performance panel: Live metrics show LCP, CLS and INP for the open page, a recorded trace shows every task on the main thread, and a long task between a click and the next paint makes the interaction slow.
explanation: The main thread runs one task at a time, so a long task holds back the paint that answers a click.

learning_check.question: What does the Performance panel show before you record anything?
learning_check.answer: Live metrics: your local LCP and CLS at once, and INP after you interact with the page.

scenes.heading: Why a click can feel slow
scenes.narration: A click feels slow when the main thread is busy. The Performance panel shows why.

visual.subtitle: Live metrics, traces and long tasks

scenes.heading: Live metrics first
scenes.narration: Open the Performance panel. Live metrics show your local LCP and CLS at once. Click on the page, and INP appears too.

items: LCP and CLS show at once

scenes.heading: From click to paint
scenes.narration: A click starts a task on the main thread. The handler runs. Only after it ends can the browser paint the next frame.

scenes.heading: Record a trace
scenes.narration: To see the cause, record a trace. Set a CPU slowdown in Capture settings, click Record, click the page, then click Stop.

items: Click the button on the page
Click Stop and read the Main track

scenes.heading: What good looks like
scenes.narration: Good values: LCP 2.5 seconds or less, INP 200 milliseconds or less, and CLS 0.1 or less.
